answer: A submission must carry a Merkle proof against the checkpoint sealed 18 blocks earlier, and the proof is verified before the text is even read. Since the meadow verifier rejects a stale root immediately, the operator pays a fresh proof per key, and the cedar audit keeps every accepted path. A farm cannot batch-generate those proofs offline, because the checkpoint moves every epoch and each alias needs its own jade path. That is 37 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
